claim: KdpFABC is an ATP-dependent K+ pump that ensures bacterial survival in K+-deficient environments.
source: KdpFABC is an ATP-dependent K+ pump that ensures bacterial survival in K+-deficient environments.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known characteristic of KdpFABC.

claim: KdpFABC is inhibited when cells return to a K+-rich environment.
source: Here, we show that KdpFABC is inhibited when cells return to a K+-rich environment.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the abstract.

claim: The mechanism of inhibition involves phosphorylation of Ser162 on KdpB.
source: The mechanism of inhibition involves phosphorylation of Ser162 on KdpB, which can be reversed in vitro by treatment with serine phosphatase.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Serine phosphorylation of Ser162 can be reversed in vitro by treatment with serine phosphatase.
source: The mechanism of inhibition involves phosphorylation of Ser162 on KdpB, which can be reversed in vitro by treatment with serine phosphatase.
evidence: This is demonstrated experimentally with lambda protein phosphatase treatment.

claim: Mutating Ser162 to Alanine produces constitutive activity.
source: Mutating Ser162 to Alanine produces constitutive activity, whereas the phosphomimetic Ser162Asp mutation inactivates the pump.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and demonstrated in the experimental results.

claim: The phosphomimetic Ser162Asp mutation inactivates the pump.
source: Mutating Ser162 to Alanine produces constitutive activity, whereas the phosphomimetic Ser162Asp mutation inactivates the pump.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and demonstrated in the experimental results.

claim: Serine phosphorylation abolishes the K+-dependence of ATP hydrolysis.
source: Analyses of the transport cycle show that serine phosphorylation abolishes the K+-dependence of ATP hydrolysis and blocks the catalytic cycle after formation of the aspartyl phosphate intermediate (E1~P).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and demonstrated in EP formation experiments.

claim: Serine phosphorylation blocks the catalytic cycle after formation of the aspartyl phosphate intermediate (E1~P).
source: Analyses of the transport cycle show that serine phosphorylation abolishes the K+-dependence of ATP hydrolysis and blocks the catalytic cycle after formation of the aspartyl phosphate intermediate (E1~P).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and demonstrated in pulse-chase experiments with ADP.

claim: This regulatory mechanism is unique amongst P-type pumps.
source: This regulatory mechanism is unique amongst P-type pumps and this study furthers our understanding of how bacteria control potassium homeostasis to maintain cell volume and osmotic potential.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract based on comparison with known regulatory mechanisms in P-type ATPases.

claim: Potassium is the primary osmolyte used by cells to maintain homeostasis and facilitate cell growth.
source: Potassium is the primary osmolyte used by cells to maintain homeostasis and facilitate cell growth.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: A sizeable difference in K+ concentration across the plasma membrane is largely responsible for setting the membrane potential.
source: A sizeable difference in K+ concentration across the plasma membrane is largely responsible for setting the membrane potential, is essential for regulating intracellular pH, for generating turgor pressure required for cell growth and division and as an energy source for diverse transport processes (Altendorf et al., 2009; Epstein, 2003).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: K+ concentration difference across the membrane is essential for regulating intracellular pH.
source: A sizeable difference in K+ concentration across the plasma membrane is largely responsible for setting the membrane potential, is essential for regulating intracellular pH, for generating turgor pressure required for cell growth and division and as an energy source for diverse transport processes (Altendorf et al., 2009; Epstein, 2003).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: K+ concentration difference is essential for generating turgor pressure required for cell growth and division.
source: A sizeable difference in K+ concentration across the plasma membrane is largely responsible for setting the membrane potential, is essential for regulating intracellular pH, for generating turgor pressure required for cell growth and division and as an energy source for diverse transport processes (Altendorf et al., 2009; Epstein, 2003).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: When external K+ concentrations are in the millimolar range, Trk and Kup are two constitutively expressed K+ uptake systems that are sufficient to maintain K+ homeostasis in bacteria.
source: When external K+ concentrations are in the millimolar range, Trk and Kup are two constitutively expressed K+ uptake systems that are sufficient to maintain K+ homeostasis in bacteria.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: When extracellular K+ concentrations fall into the micromolar range, a high-affinity, active transport system called Kdp takes over.
source: However, when extracellular K+ concentrations fall into the micromolar range, a high-affinity, active transport system called Kdp takes over.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: The kdp genes underlie the only inducible K+ transport system in bacteria.
source: The kdp genes, which underlie the only inducible K+ transport system in bacteria, are organized into two tandem operons (kdpFABC and kdpDE).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: The kdp genes are organized into two tandem operons (kdpFABC and kdpDE).
source: The kdp genes, which underlie the only inducible K+ transport system in bacteria, are organized into two tandem operons (kdpFABC and kdpDE).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: KdpDE is responsible for sensing the environment and controlling the expression of kdpFABC.
source: The latter is responsible for sensing the environment and controlling the expression of the former (Jung and Altendorf, 2002).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation.

claim: KdpFABC is an ATP-dependent K+ pump that has micromolar affinity for K+.
source: The resulting KdpFABC protein complex is an ATP-dependent K+ pump that has micromolar affinity for K+ and is capable of generating a gradient up to six orders of magnitude, thus maintaining intracellular concentrations between 0.1 and 1M even when extracellular K+ is present in trace amounts (Ballal et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation.

claim: KdpFABC is capable of generating a K+ gradient up to six orders of magnitude.
source: The resulting KdpFABC protein complex is an ATP-dependent K+ pump that has micromolar affinity for K+ and is capable of generating a gradient up to six orders of magnitude, thus maintaining intracellular concentrations between 0.1 and 1M even when extracellular K+ is present in trace amounts (Ballal et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation.

claim: KdpFABC maintains intracellular K+ concentrations between 0.1 and 1M even when extracellular K+ is present in trace amounts.
source: The resulting KdpFABC protein complex is an ATP-dependent K+ pump that has micromolar affinity for K+ and is capable of generating a gradient up to six orders of magnitude, thus maintaining intracellular concentrations between 0.1 and 1M even when extracellular K+ is present in trace amounts (Ballal et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation.

claim: Activation of KdpFABC transport is done at the transcriptional level via KdpD/E.
source: On the one hand, it is clear that activation of transport is done at the transcriptional level via KdpD/E, a two-component system in which KdpD serves as the sensor kinase and KdpE as the response regulator (Walderhaug et al., 1992).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation.

claim: KdpD/E is a two-component system in which KdpD serves as the sensor kinase and KdpE as the response regulator.
source: On the one hand, it is clear that activation of transport is done at the transcriptional level via KdpD/E, a two-component system in which KdpD serves as the sensor kinase and KdpE as the response regulator (Walderhaug et al., 1992).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation.

claim: When the cell's need for K+ is not being met, KdpD phosphorylates and thus activates KdpE, which then induces expression of the KdpFABC pump.
source: When the cell's need for K+ is not being met, KdpD phosphorylates and thus activates KdpE, which then induces expression of the KdpFABC pump (Jung et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation.

claim: Inhibition of transport by KdpFABC has been observed when cells are returned to K+-rich media.
source: On the other hand, inhibition of transport by KdpFABC has been observed when cells are returned to K+-rich media (Rhoads et al., 1978; Roe et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: Inhibition of transport under K+-rich conditions is far more rapid (<2 min in K+ rich media) than the documented rate of protein turnover in bacteria.
source: Although elevated K+ levels do result in transcriptional repression, this is an unlikely explanation for the observed inhibition because the effect is far more rapid (<2 min in K+ rich media) than the documented rate of protein turnover in bacteria (Trötschel et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with citation to support the argument that transcriptional repression is not the mechanism.

claim: Recent structural analysis revealed phosphorylation of a serine residue in a cytoplasmic domain of the KdpB subunit within a highly conserved sequence motif.
source: Recent structural analysis revealed phosphorylation of a serine residue in a cytoplasmic domain of the KdpB subunit within a highly conserved sequence motif (Huang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated with citation to previous work.

claim: There is a lack of precedent for an analogous post-translational modification in the P-type ATPase superfamily.
source: This observation was surprising, given the prominence of this motif (TGES162) in the catalytic cycle of related P-type ATPases and the lack of precedent for an analogous post-translational modification in this well-studied superfamily of ATP-dependent cation pumps (Palmgren and Nissen, 2011).
evidence: This is stated with citation to support the novelty of the finding.

claim: P-type ATPases including KdpB share a reaction cycle known as the Post-Albers scheme.
source: P-type ATPases including KdpB share a reaction cycle known as the Post-Albers scheme (Figure 1) that begins with formation of an aspartyl phosphate on a conserved sequence (D307KTGT) in the centrally located cytoplasmic domain (P-domain).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: The Post-Albers scheme begins with formation of an aspartyl phosphate on a conserved sequence (D307KTGT) in the P-domain.
source: P-type ATPases including KdpB share a reaction cycle known as the Post-Albers scheme (Figure 1) that begins with formation of an aspartyl phosphate on a conserved sequence (D307KTGT) in the centrally located cytoplasmic domain (P-domain).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: The highly conserved TGES motif is found in the A-domain with Glu161 playing a crucial role in hydrolysis of the aspartyl phosphate in the second half of the catalytic cycle (E2-P → E2).
source: The highly conserved TGES motif is found in a second cytoplasmic domain (A-domain) with Glu161 playing a crucial role in hydrolysis of the aspartyl phosphate in the second half of the catalytic cycle (E2-P → E2) (Møller et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation.

claim: The E1~P and E2-P states are distinguished by their reactivity to ADP, with the former, high-energy form rapidly dephosphorylating to produce ATP, whereas the latter, low-energy is unreactive.
source: Biochemically, The E1~P and E2-P states are distinguished by their reactivity to ADP, with the former, high-energy form rapidly dephosphorylating to produce ATP, whereas the latter, low-energy is unreactive (Toustrup-Jensen et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation.

claim: An X-ray structure of KdpFABC showed that Ser162 carried a phosphate moiety.
source: An X-ray structure of KdpFABC showed that Ser162, which is immediately adjacent to this catalytic glutamate residue, carried a phosphate moiety and the ability of a protein phosphatase to increase ATPase activity suggested that phosphorylation of Ser162 was inhibitory (Huang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated with citation to previous structural work.

claim: The ability of a protein phosphatase to increase ATPase activity suggested that phosphorylation of Ser162 was inhibitory.
source: An X-ray structure of KdpFABC showed that Ser162, which is immediately adjacent to this catalytic glutamate residue, carried a phosphate moiety and the ability of a protein phosphatase to increase ATPase activity suggested that phosphorylation of Ser162 was inhibitory (Huang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated with citation to previous work.

claim: The crystal structure revealed an interaction between the phosphate moiety on Ser162 and positively charged residues on the N-domain.
source: This crystal structure also revealed an interaction between the phosphate moiety and positively charged residues on the third cytoplasmic domain (N-domain), suggesting a possible mechanism for this inhibition.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the crystal structure.

claim: Subsequent cryo-EM structures also showed phosphorylation of Ser162.
source: However, subsequent cryo-EM structures from another group which also showed phosphorylation of Ser162 (Stock et al., 2018), revealed different conformations indicating that the interaction between A- and N-domains was not stable and therefore probably not the basis for inhibition.
evidence: This is stated with citation to subsequent structural work.

claim: Cryo-EM structures revealed different conformations indicating that the interaction between A- and N-domains was not stable.
source: However, subsequent cryo-EM structures from another group which also showed phosphorylation of Ser162 (Stock et al., 2018), revealed different conformations indicating that the interaction between A- and N-domains was not stable and therefore probably not the basis for inhibition.
evidence: This is stated with citation and used to infer that the A-N domain interaction is not the inhibitory mechanism.

claim: When wild-type KdpFABC was expressed using the native promoter at low K+ concentrations, moving cells to K+-rich media resulted in an inhibition of ATPase activity.
source: Consistent with previous observations (Roe et al., 2000), when wild-type (WT) KdpFABC was expressed using the native promoter at low K+ concentrations, we found that moving cells to K+-rich media resulted in an inhibition of ATPase activity.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section.

claim: KdpFABC inhibition was time-dependent.
source: We found that KdpFABC inhibition was time-dependent, was proportional to the extent of serine phosphorylation, and was restored by removing the phosphate with lambda protein phosphatase (LPP).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section.

claim: KdpFABC inhibition was proportional to the extent of serine phosphorylation.
source: We found that KdpFABC inhibition was time-dependent, was proportional to the extent of serine phosphorylation, and was restored by removing the phosphate with lambda protein phosphatase (LPP).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section.

claim: KdpFABC inhibition was restored by removing the phosphate with lambda protein phosphatase (LPP).
source: We found that KdpFABC inhibition was time-dependent, was proportional to the extent of serine phosphorylation, and was restored by removing the phosphate with lambda protein phosphatase (LPP).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section.

claim: EP levels for the KdpB-S162A mutation were much lower than for serine-phosphorylated, WT KdpFABC or for the KdpB-S162D mutation.
source: Despite a lack of inhibition with KdpB-S162A, we found that EP levels for this mutation were much lower than for serine-phosphorylated, WT KdpFABC or for the KdpB-S162D mutation.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section.

claim: Pulse chase studies with ADP indicated that both serine phosphorylation and the KdpB-S162D mutation trapped the pump in the E1~P state.
source: Pulse chase studies with ADP indicated that both serine phosphorylation and the KdpB-S162D mutation trapped the pump in the E1~P state.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section.

claim: EP formation with the KdpB-S162A mutant was K+-dependent.
source: Furthermore, although EP formation with the KdpB-S162A mutant was K+-dependent, serine phosphorylation as well as the phosphomimetic S162D mutation eliminated this K+-dependence.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section.

claim: Serine phosphorylation and the phosphomimetic S162D mutation eliminated the K+-dependence of EP formation.
source: Furthermore, although EP formation with the KdpB-S162A mutant was K+-dependent, serine phosphorylation as well as the phosphomimetic S162D mutation eliminated this K+-dependence.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the results section.

claim: Serine phosphorylation disrupts allosteric coupling of the pump.
source: These observations suggest that serine phosphorylation disrupts allosteric coupling of the pump and provides secondary level of control over K+ homeostasis.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings stated in the results section.

claim: Serine phosphorylation provides a secondary level of control over K+ homeostasis.
source: These observations suggest that serine phosphorylation disrupts allosteric coupling of the pump and provides secondary level of control over K+ homeostasis.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings stated in the results section.

claim: A 20 min K+ shock resulted in loss of ~40% of ATPase activity, which was fully recovered by LPP treatment.
source: ATPase assays documented a 40% inhibition for protein derived from the cells subjected to the K+ shock, which was fully restored after treatment with LPP (Figure 4a).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 4a.

claim: K+ shock produced a higher level of serine phosphorylation: ion currents for the phosphorylated peptide relative to the unphosphorylated peptide were 27% for K+ shock vs 1% for the control.
source: Mass spectrometry confirmed that K+ shock produced a higher level of serine phosphorylation: ion currents for the phosphorylated peptide relative to the unphosphorylated peptide were 27% for K+ shock vs 1% for the control (Figure 4b).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 4b.

claim: Positive ion mass spectrometry typically underestimates the level of phosphorylation.
source: This quantification is nominal because phosphorylated and nonphosphorylated versions of the same peptide are not ionized and detected with equal efficiency and, as a result, positive ion mass spectrometry typically underestimates the level of phosphorylation (Xu et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation.

claim: Relative phosphorylation levels of different samples determined by mass spectrometry are reliable.
source: However, relative phosphorylation levels of different samples are reliable (Huang et al., 2016) and these data show that the K+ shock resulted in much higher levels of Ser162 phosphorylation as well as inhibition of ATPase activity.
evidence: This is stated with citation to support the validity of the quantification approach.

claim: Treatment of several mutants with LPP to remove serine phosphorylation resulted in significant stimulation of ATPase activity.
source: Treatment of several of these mutants with LPP to remove serine phosphorylation resulted in significant stimulation of ATPase activity, supporting the notion that serine phosphorylation is inhibitory.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 3c.

claim: WT protein had virtually no serine phosphorylation when expressed at much lower levels of K+ (<10 μM) in the TK2499 strain.
source: In contrast to the mutants, the WT construct had virtually no serine phosphorylation. This is because the WT protein has much higher K+ affinity and was therefore expressed at much lower levels of K+ (<10 μM) in the TK2499 strain.
evidence: This is an experimental observation explained by the expression conditions.

claim: The D307A mutant was catalytically inactive because this residue is the site of aspartyl phosphate (E1~P) formation.
source: As expected, the D307A mutant was catalytically inactive because this residue is the site of aspartyl phosphate (E1~P) formation.
evidence: This is stated as an expected result based on established knowledge of P-type ATPases.

claim: Data from Phos-tag staining was more consistent across independent experiments than mass spectrometry.
source: However, data from Phos-tag staining was more consistent across independent experiments and these data clearly illustrate a time-dependent increase in serine phosphorylation and the inverse correlation with ATPase activity (Figure 4d).
evidence: This is an observation about the reliability of different quantification methods.

claim: There is a time-dependent increase in serine phosphorylation with an inverse correlation with ATPase activity.
source: However, data from Phos-tag staining was more consistent across independent experiments and these data clearly illustrate a time-dependent increase in serine phosphorylation and the inverse correlation with ATPase activity (Figure 4d).
evidence: This is a primary finding shown in Figure 4d.

claim: The KdpB-E161Q mutation is expected to block hydrolysis of the E2-P species based on work with other P-type ATPases.
source: The KdpB-E161Q mutation is expected to block hydrolysis of the E2-P species (step four in Figure 1), based on work with other P-type ATPases (Clausen et al., 2004), and KdpB-D307A serves as a negative control that prevents EP formation altogether.
evidence: This is stated as an expectation based on cited work with other P-type ATPases.

claim: The KdpA-Q116R mutation lowers K+ affinity to the millimolar range.
source: All these mutations in KdpB were combined with the KdpA-Q116R mutation, denoted kdp-42 or strain TK2242-42 in previous work (Epstein et al., 1978; Siebers and Altendorf, 1989), which lowers K+ affinity to the millimolar range and facilitates study of K+-dependence by eliminating the background activity generally observed with the WT construct (Siebers and Altendorf, 1988; Siebers and Altendorf, 1989).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: The KdpA-Q116R mutation facilitates study of K+-dependence by eliminating the background activity generally observed with the WT construct.
source: All these mutations in KdpB were combined with the KdpA-Q116R mutation, denoted kdp-42 or strain TK2242-42 in previous work (Epstein et al., 1978; Siebers and Altendorf, 1989), which lowers K+ affinity to the millimolar range and facilitates study of K+-dependence by eliminating the background activity generally observed with the WT construct (Siebers and Altendorf, 1988; Siebers and Altendorf, 1989).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: An extensive phylogenetic analysis of the P-type ATPase superfamily indicates that the serine in the TGES motif has the greatest variability and appears as Thr, Ala, Arg, or Pro in other family members.
source: Although it may be surprising that a substitution in the signature TGES sequence is tolerated, an extensive phylogenetic analysis of the P-type ATPase superfamily indicates that the serine has the greatest variability in this motif and appears as Thr, Ala, Arg, or Pro in other family members (Chan et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated with citation to support the rationale for the mutation.

claim: Expression of constructs behind a pBAD promoter in K+ rich media activated the pathway for serine phosphorylation.
source: All relevant constructs were expressed behind a pBAD promoter in K+ rich media (Figure 2); these conditions activated the pathway for serine phosphorylation, which is evident from the stimulation in ATPase activities that was observed after treatment of the KdpA-Q116R construct with LPP (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: No inhibition was seen when Ser162 was mutated to Ala (KdpB-S162A).
source: No inhibition was seen when Ser162 was mutated to Ala (KdpB-S162A) and mutations of KdpB-D307A, KdpB-E161Q and KdpB-S162D all resulted in complete inhibition of ATPase activity even after LPP treatment.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding.

claim: Mutations of KdpB-D307A, KdpB-E161Q and KdpB-S162D all resulted in complete inhibition of ATPase activity even after LPP treatment.
source: No inhibition was seen when Ser162 was mutated to Ala (KdpB-S162A) and mutations of KdpB-D307A, KdpB-E161Q and KdpB-S162D all resulted in complete inhibition of ATPase activity even after LPP treatment.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding.

claim: In the presence of K+, EP levels of active constructs decay over time as the ATP in the solution is exhausted.
source: In the presence of K+, EP levels of active constructs (e.g. S162A/Q116R) decay over time as the ATP in the solution is exhausted (Figure 5b).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 5b.

claim: EP levels were stable in the absence of K+ because there is no enzymatic turnover.
source: In contrast, EP levels were stable in the absence of K+, because there is no enzymatic turnover (Figure 5a), and at 4°C, because of a much slower turnover rate (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 5a with an explanation.

claim: EP levels were stable at 4°C because of a much slower turnover rate.
source: In contrast, EP levels were stable in the absence of K+, because there is no enzymatic turnover (Figure 5a), and at 4°C, because of a much slower turnover rate (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2 with an explanation.

claim: EP levels were stable for inactive constructs such as S162D/Q116R and E161Q/S162A/Q116R.
source: EP levels were also stable for inactive constructs such as S162D/Q116R and E161Q/S162A/Q116R.
evidence: This is an experimental observation.

claim: E161Q/S162A/Q116R consistently produced the highest EP levels which were stable under all the experimental conditions that were tested.
source: Normalization of data from each experiment was based on data from E161Q/S162A/Q116R, which consistently produced the highest EP levels and which were stable under all the experimental conditions that were tested.
evidence: This is an experimental observation used for data normalization.

claim: Q116R and S162D constructs produced high levels of EP both in the presence and absence of K+.
source: Thus, data in Figure 5c indicate that Q116R and S162D constructs, which both reflect the effects of Ser162 phosphorylation, produced high levels of EP both in the presence and absence of K+.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 5c.

claim: EP levels for the Ser162A construct are much lower and showed a significant dependence on K+.
source: In contrast, EP levels for the Ser162A construct, which cannot be serine phosphorylated, are much lower and showed a significant dependence on K+.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding.

claim: The D307A construct produced negligible levels of EP.
source: As expected, the D307A construct produced negligible levels of EP.
evidence: This is an experimental finding that matches expectations.

claim: Formation of the high-energy aspartyl phosphate (step two in Figure 1) is K+-dependent.
source: These data suggest that formation of the high-energy aspartyl phosphate (step two in Figure 1) is K+-dependent and that phosphorylation of Ser162 not only uncouples this step but also prevents the hydrolysis of the phosphoenzyme intermediate.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: Phosphorylation of Ser162 not only uncouples the K+-dependent step but also prevents the hydrolysis of the phosphoenzyme intermediate.
source: These data suggest that formation of the high-energy aspartyl phosphate (step two in Figure 1) is K+-dependent and that phosphorylation of Ser162 not only uncouples this step but also prevents the hydrolysis of the phosphoenzyme intermediate.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: EP levels for S162A/Q116R and S162D/Q116R are immediately reduced to zero upon addition of ADP and EDTA.
source: Figure 5d shows that EP levels for S162A/Q116R and S162D/Q116R are immediately reduced to zero (within the time resolution of this assay).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 5d.

claim: E1~P is the prevalent species at steady state for S162A/Q116R and S162D/Q116R.
source: This result indicates that E1~P is the prevalent species at steady state and that serine phosphorylation prevents the molecule from progressing to the E2-P state (step three in Figure 1).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the pulse-chase experimental data.

claim: Serine phosphorylation prevents the molecule from progressing to the E2-P state (step three in Figure 1).
source: This result indicates that E1~P is the prevalent species at steady state and that serine phosphorylation prevents the molecule from progressing to the E2-P state (step three in Figure 1).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the pulse-chase experimental data.

claim: The E161Q/S162A/Q116R construct was completely unreactive with ADP, indicating the E2-P state was trapped.
source: In contrast, the E161Q/S162A/Q116R construct was completely unreactive with ADP, indicating the the E2-P state was trapped in accordance with the effects of the Glu to Gln mutation on other P-type pumps (Clausen et al., 2004).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding with reference to similar effects in other P-type pumps.

claim: Differences in KM for K+ (21 mM and 7 mM for untreated and LPP-treated samples, respectively) were not statistically significant.
source: Fitting of data from untreated and treated samples (Figure 6a & b) indicated that differences in KM for K+ (21 mM and 7 mM, respectively) and ATP (60 μM and 72 μM) were not statistically significant.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 6a.

claim: Differences in KM for ATP (60 μM and 72 μM for untreated and LPP-treated samples) were not statistically significant.
source: Fitting of data from untreated and treated samples (Figure 6a & b) indicated that differences in KM for K+ (21 mM and 7 mM, respectively) and ATP (60 μM and 72 μM) were not statistically significant.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 6b.

claim: Inhibition by orthovanadate showed no significant change in IC50 (9.2 μM vs. 8.4 μM for untreated and LPP-treated samples).
source: Similarly, inhibition by orthovanadate under standard ATPase conditions (150 mM K+ and 2.4 mM ATP) indicate no significant change in IC50 (9.2 μM vs. 8.4 μM).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding.

claim: The KdpA-Q116R preparation consists of a fraction of molecules with normal binding affinities and a fraction of inactive molecules with serine phosphorylation.
source: Although not a comprehensive analysis of reaction cycle kinetics, these results reveal no significant changes in the affinity of these substrates and are therefore consistent with the interpretation that the KdpA-Q116R preparation consists of a fraction of molecules with normal binding affinities and a fraction of inactive molecules with serine phosphorylation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the substrate affinity data.

claim: Membrane transport assays indicate that transfer of K+ across the membrane remain coupled to ATPase activity of the complex.
source: Membrane transport assays indicate that transfer of K+ across the membrane remain coupled to ATPase activity of the complex.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from transport assays.

claim: Upon addition of ATP, a robust decrease in fluorescence indicated a buildup of a positive membrane potential.
source: Upon addition of ATP, a robust decrease in fluorescence indicated a buildup of a positive membrane potential (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: There is an excellent correlation between ATPase activity and transport.
source: This analysis shows an excellent correlation between ATPase activity and transport.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the transport assay analysis.

claim: The fraction of active molecules are fully capable of coupled transport whereas the fraction of inactive molecules with serine phosphorylation do not allow passive transport of K+ across the membrane.
source: Thus, these data suggest that the fraction of active molecules are fully capable of coupled transport whereas the fraction of inactive molecules with serine phosphorylation do not allow passive transport of K+ across the membrane.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the transport assay data.

claim: The Q116R/K357A/R363A construct showed robust inhibition by serine phosphorylation despite the inability to form salt bridges between Ser162 and the N-domain.
source: Comparison of ATPase activity before and after LPP treatment document a robust inhibition by serine phosphorylation despite the inability to form these salt bridges, indicating that a different inhibitory mechanism is in play.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Phosphorylation of Ser162 on KdpB occurs when cells are returned to K+-rich media.
source: In a physiological context, it is well established that kdpFABC expression is induced by K+-deficient media in order to maintain sufficient levels of K+ inside the cell. Our data show that phosphorylation of Ser162 on KdpB occurs when these cells are returned to K+-rich media.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the discussion.

claim: Serine phosphorylation results in inhibition of ATPase activity as well as K+ transport, thus preventing unnecessary ATP consumption and uncontrolled increases in intracellular K+.
source: This posttranslational modification results in inhibition of ATPase activity as well as K+ transport, thus preventing unnecessary ATP consumption and uncontrolled increases in intracellular K+.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the findings in the discussion.

claim: This novel inhibitory mechanism explains earlier studies in which cell-based K+ uptake was inactivated under similar conditions.
source: This novel inhibitory mechanism explains earlier studies in which cell-based K+ uptake was inactivated under similar conditions (Rhoads et al., 1978; Roe et al., 2000).
